title: Finding sides and angles
objectives: Find a missing side of a right-angled triangle with sine, cosine or tangent
Find a missing angle with an inverse ratio

screens.title: Finding sides and angles
screens.prose: A ratio and one side are enough to find another side. Two sides are enough to find the angle. We will use both directions.
You stand 20 m from a tree. A clinometer says the treetop is $35^\circ$ above level. Your calculator gives $\tan 35^\circ \approx 0.700$. The slider sets the tree's height.
screens.question: Slide the height until up ÷ across matches $\tan 35^\circ$.

hints.text: Tangent is opposite over adjacent: height over 20.
Watch the caption, not the picture: it must read 0.700.
Height ÷ 20 = 0.700 means height = 20 × 0.700 = 14 m.

feedback.correct: $14 \div 20 = 0.700$, so the tree is 14 m tall.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Slide until the caption reads 0.700.

byKey.sine: Near 11.5 m you have height = $20 \times \sin 35^\circ$. The 20 m is the ground, the adjacent side, so tangent is the ratio.
byKey.equal: Height 20 makes up equal to across, which is $45^\circ$. The angle here is only $35^\circ$.

explain.text: You matched $\tfrac{h}{20}$ to $\tan 35^\circ$, which is the same as $h = 20 \tan 35^\circ \approx 14.0$ m. Rearranging the ratio finds the side in one step.

screens.prose: A 6 m ladder leans on a wall at $70^\circ$ to the ground. The ladder is the hypotenuse. Your calculator gives $\sin 70^\circ \approx 0.9397$.
screens.question: How high up the wall does the ladder reach? Give 2 decimal places.

hints.text: The height is opposite the $70^\circ$ angle, and the ladder is the hypotenuse.
Opposite and hypotenuse: that pair is the sine.
$\sin 70^\circ = \tfrac{h}{6}$, so $h = 6 \times 0.9397$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write $\sin 70^\circ = \tfrac{h}{6}$ and solve for $h$.

byKey.divided: You divided 6 by the sine. The unknown is on top of the fraction, so multiply.
byKey.cos: That is $6 \cos 70^\circ$, the distance along the ground. The wall is opposite the angle.
byKey.tan: Tangent needs the adjacent side, which is not known here. The ladder is the hypotenuse.

explain.text: $\sin 70^\circ = \tfrac{h}{6}$, so $h = 6 \sin 70^\circ \approx 5.64$ m. A sanity check: the height is less than the ladder, as it must be.

screens.prose: A kite flies 30 m above the ground. Its taut string makes $40^\circ$ with the ground. Now the unknown is the hypotenuse. Your calculator gives $\sin 40^\circ \approx 0.6428$.
screens.question: How long is the string? Give 2 decimal places.

widget.label: Length of the string, in metres

hints.text: Write the sine ratio with the string as $s$.
Opposite is 30 m and the string is the hypotenuse.
$0.6428 = \tfrac{30}{s}$. Multiply both sides by $s$, then divide by 0.6428.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The unknown is on the bottom: $\sin 40^\circ = \tfrac{30}{s}$.

byKey.multiplied: You multiplied 30 by the sine, as on the last screen. Here the unknown is the bottom of the fraction, so divide.
byKey.cos: You divided by the cosine. The 30 m faces the angle, so the ratio is the sine.
byKey.ground: That is $30 \div \tan 40^\circ$, the distance along the ground, not the string.

explain.text: $\sin 40^\circ = \tfrac{30}{s}$, so $s = \tfrac{30}{\sin 40^\circ} \approx 46.67$ m. The string is longer than the height, which checks out. When the unknown sits on the bottom, you divide.

screens.prose: A plank rests at $25^\circ$ to the floor. It covers 3 m of floor from end to end underneath. We want the plank's length.
screens.question: Which ratio links the side you know to the side you want?

options.why: Sine needs the side facing the angle. The 3 m of floor touches the angle: it is adjacent.
Tangent leaves the hypotenuse out, but the plank is the hypotenuse.
That puts the hypotenuse on top, which would make the cosine bigger than 1.

hints.text: Name the two sides from the $25^\circ$ angle.
The floor touches the angle; the plank faces the right angle.
Adjacent and hypotenuse belong together in cosine.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Label the 3 m and the plank from the angle, then pick the ratio holding both.

explain.text: The 3 m is adjacent and the plank is the hypotenuse, so $\cos 25^\circ = \tfrac{3}{\text{plank}}$. Then plank $= \tfrac{3}{\cos 25^\circ} \approx \tfrac{3}{0.9063} \approx 3.31$ m. Pick the ratio by the two sides involved: the one you know and the one you want.

screens.prose: Now the sides are known and the angle is not. This ramp rises 1.5 m over 4 m. The slider turns a line about O, and its angle is shown in degrees.
screens.question: Turn the line until it runs along OB.

hints.text: The line should pass exactly through B.
B sits 1.5 above A.
$\tan\theta = \tfrac{1.5}{4} = 0.375$. Look for the angle with that tangent: between $20^\circ$ and $21^\circ$.

feedback.correct: The line lies along OB at about $20.6^\circ$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Turn the line until it passes through B.

byKey.steep: The line now passes above B. Turn it back down towards the ramp.

explain.text: You searched for the angle whose tangent is $\tfrac{1.5}{4} = 0.375$. The calculator's inverse tangent does that search in one press: $\tan^{-1}(0.375) \approx 20.56^\circ$. $\sin^{-1}$ and $\cos^{-1}$ undo sine and cosine the same way.

screens.prose: A 5 m ladder reaches 4.2 m up a wall. We want the angle $\theta$ it makes with the ground.
screens.question: Find $\theta$ in degrees, to 1 decimal place.

widget.label: Angle with the ground, in degrees

hints.text: Which two sides do you know, seen from $\theta$?
4.2 m is opposite $\theta$ and the 5 m ladder is the hypotenuse.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Form the sine from the two known sides, then take the inverse sine.

byKey.tan: That is $\tan^{-1}(0.84)$. The 5 m is the hypotenuse, so the ratio is the sine.
byKey.cos: That is $\cos^{-1}(0.84)$, the angle at the top of the ladder. The wall faces $\theta$, so use sine.
byKey.ratio: 0.84 is $\sin\theta$. Take the inverse sine to turn it into an angle.

explain.text: $\sin\theta = \tfrac{4.2}{5} = 0.84$, and $\sin^{-1}(0.84) \approx 57.1^\circ$. The top angle is $90^\circ - 57.1^\circ = 32.9^\circ$, which is $\cos^{-1}(0.84)$.

screens.prose: A wheelchair ramp climbs at $15^\circ$ and covers 12 m of ground. How high is its top end? Calculator values: $\sin 15^\circ \approx 0.2588$, $\cos 15^\circ \approx 0.9659$, $\tan 15^\circ \approx 0.2679$.
screens.question: How high is the top of the ramp?

options.why: You used sine with the 12 m, treating the ground as the hypotenuse. The sloping ramp is the hypotenuse; the ground is adjacent.
You divided 12 by $\tan 15^\circ$. The height is on top of the ratio, so multiply.
That is $12 \div \cos 15^\circ$, the length of the sloping ramp, not its height.

hints.text: Is the 12 m the hypotenuse?
The ground touches the angle and is not the hypotenuse: it is adjacent.
Opposite and adjacent: $\tan 15^\circ = \tfrac{h}{12}$, so $h = 12 \times 0.2679$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Label the 12 m and the height from the $15^\circ$ angle first.

byKey.sin: You used sine, as if the 12 m of ground were the hypotenuse. The hypotenuse faces the right angle: it is the ramp itself.

explain.text: The 12 m of ground is adjacent and the height is opposite, so $h = 12 \tan 15^\circ \approx 3.22$ m. Sine would need the sloping length, about 12.42 m. The answers are close here only because the angle is small.

screens.prose: Every side problem runs through the same four moves. Put them in order for the ramp you just solved: 12 m of ground, angle $15^\circ$, height $h$.
screens.question: Put the steps in order.

lines.text: Label from the $15^\circ$ angle: 12 is adjacent, $h$ is opposite
Evaluate and check: $h \approx 3.22$ m, less than the 12 m

hints.text: You cannot pick a ratio before the sides have names.
Start from the angle, then the sides around it.
Label, pick the ratio, rearrange, evaluate.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The labels decide the ratio, and the ratio comes before the rearranging.

byKey.pick: The ratio depends on the labels, so labelling comes first.
byKey.solve: You rearrange an equation, so the ratio has to be written first.

explain.text: The labels choose the ratio, the ratio gives an equation, and the equation is rearranged. For an angle, the last two moves become an inverse: $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\tfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}\right)$.

screens.prose: A trend line on a daily chart gains £4.00 over 5 days. The chart is drawn with square units: one day across is as long as £1.00 up.
screens.question: What angle does the trend line make with the time axis, in degrees to 1 decimal place?

widget.label: Angle of the trend line, in degrees

hints.text: The gradient is up ÷ across: £4.00 per 5 days.
The rise is opposite the angle and the run is adjacent.
$\tan\theta = \tfrac{4}{5} = 0.8$, so $\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.8)$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The gradient is the tangent of the angle; undo it with $\tan^{-1}$.

byKey.flipped: You used across ÷ up, which gives the angle with the price axis. The rise goes on top.
byKey.gradient: 0.8 is the gradient, the tangent of the angle. Take $\tan^{-1}$ to get degrees.
byKey.sine: That is $\sin^{-1}(0.8)$. The 5 days are the adjacent side, not the hypotenuse.

explain.text: The gradient $\tfrac{4}{5} = 0.8$ is $\tan\theta$, so $\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.8) \approx 38.7^\circ$. Stretch the price axis and the drawn angle changes, but the gradient does not. That is why analysts quote gradients rather than chart angles.

ideas: Label the sides from the angle, then pick the ratio that holds the side you know and the side you want.
If the unknown is on top of the ratio, multiply; if it is on the bottom, divide.
To find an angle, form the ratio from two sides and undo it with $\sin^{-1}$, $\cos^{-1}$ or $\tan^{-1}$.

formula.name: Finding an angle
formula.note: An angle of elevation is measured up from the level. A sine or cosine above 1 means the sides are impossible.

summary.trap: Sine and cosine need the hypotenuse. If the side you know lies along the ground beside the angle, it is adjacent, not the hypotenuse.

quiz.prose: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 8 and an angle of $25^\circ$. Use $\cos 25^\circ \approx 0.9063$ and $\sin 25^\circ \approx 0.4226$.
quiz.question: How long is the side adjacent to the $25^\circ$ angle?

options.why: You divided by the cosine. The unknown is on top of the ratio, so multiply.
Tangent does not involve the hypotenuse, which is the side you know.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Adjacent and hypotenuse go together in cosine.

quiz.prose: A right-angled triangle has opposite side 7 and adjacent side 10 for the angle $\theta$.
quiz.question: Find $\theta$ in degrees, to 1 decimal place.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Opposite over adjacent is the tangent.

byKey.flipped: You found $\tan^{-1}(\tfrac{10}{7})$, the other acute angle. Opposite goes on top.
byKey.sine: That is $\sin^{-1}(0.7)$. Neither side is the hypotenuse, so use tangent.
byKey.cosine: That is $\cos^{-1}(0.7)$. Neither side is the hypotenuse.

quiz.prose: Someone wants a 3 m ladder to reach a window 3.5 m up a wall.
quiz.question: At what angle to the ground should they set it?

options.text: No angle works: $\sin\theta$ would be about 1.17

options.why: Even upright, a 3 m ladder reaches only 3 m. The height can never beat the hypotenuse.
That treats the ladder as the ground side. The ladder is the hypotenuse, and it is shorter than the height.

feedback.correct: The ladder is shorter than the height, so no triangle exists.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the height with the ladder's length.

explain.text: We would need $\sin\theta = \tfrac{3.5}{3} \approx 1.17$. But a sine is never more than 1, and a calculator shows an error for $\sin^{-1}(1.17)$. That is the edge case: the opposite side cannot exceed the hypotenuse.

quiz.prose: From 50 m away on level ground, the top of a building is $32^\circ$ above level. Use $\tan 32^\circ \approx 0.6249$.
quiz.question: How tall is the building, to 2 decimal places?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The 50 m is adjacent and the height is opposite.

byKey.sine: You used sine, treating the 50 m as the hypotenuse. The line of sight is the hypotenuse.
byKey.divided: You divided by the tangent. The height is on top, so multiply.
byKey.cosine: Cosine pairs the 50 m with the line of sight, not the height.

explain.text: The angle of elevation sits at your eye. The ground is adjacent and the height opposite, so $h = 50 \tan 32^\circ \approx 31.24$ m.
